label: Unexplained absence: lacking a determination an admissible profile adds to all one has
definition: UnexplainedAbsence Admissible Has x k: x lacks k, and some admissible profile contains every real determination of x together with k. Then neither the admissibility constraints (no admissible profile contains k) nor x's positive profile (no admissible profile contains its determinations and k) fixes the omission. It is not a claim that the absence has no truthmaker, cause or totality fact; it says only that the two represented intrinsic explanations leave it open.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145), attribution deferred. Absence from the constraints is AbsenceFromAdmissibility and absence from the positive profile is AbsenceFromPositiveProfile; absenceTrichotomy proves, with excluded middle, that every absence is exactly one of the three relative to one family. A primitive totality or closure fact of the bearer, if not represented in the family, leaves an absence unexplained in this sense; denying NoUnexplainedAbsenceAtRoots is the way to hold such a fact. Extrinsic explanation by a ground is not represented because an actual root has no actual concrete ground.
